newsitem.title: DUBAI: Oman and Iran to develop offshore gas field.
newsitem.headline: Oman and Iran to develop offshore gas field.

text.p: Oman and Iran have agreed in principle to select firms to develop their shared offshore Henjam gas and condensate field in the Strait of Hormuz, the Oman News Agency (ONA) reported on Sunday.
"(Oman and Iran) agreed in principle to choose international firms to upgrade, utilise and develop the field," ONA said.
Henjam straddles the maritime border between the two oil producers and Iranian officials have estimated the field's gas reserves at one trillion cubic feet (30 billion cubic metres).
Gas and condensate is already produced from the Omani side of the shared field -- where it is known as the Bukha field -- and exports are sent by pipeline to the United Arab Emirates.

The ONA report gave no details on the potential capacity of the shared field when developed, financing arrangements or when Henjam would come stream though analysts estimate that full development would take three years.
The two countries set up a joint ministerial committee to study the field's development in 1990 and agreed in 1995 to jointly develop the field.
Henjam was first discovered in 1976 and Bukha in 1979.
